newsitem.title: UK: British Airways outlines strike plan.
newsitem.headline: British Airways outlines strike plan.

text.p: British Airways on Sunday issued details of the flights it says it will continue to operate if cabin crew go ahead with planned three-day strikes from Wednesday.
The announcement followed the breakdown of talks with the cabin crews' Transport and General Workers' Union (T&G) in a dispute over pay and conditions.
The worst-affected flights will be BA intercontinental services from London's Heathrow and Gatwick Airports and its European services out of Heathrow.
The airline said in a statement that all its domestic and European flights from Gatwick would continue to operate as would international flights from regional airports in the United Kingdom.
All services operated by BA's franchise and alliance partners would also continue through the threatened strike, the statement said.

It said that out of Heathrow, BA would operate almost half of its intercontinental flights and around a quarter of European services, while around one third of intercontinental flights from Gatwick would go ahead.
Customers booked onto cancelled BA flights would be offered flights on the nearest alternative days, offered a full refund or, where possible, transferred to other airlines, BA said.

"We know how worrying and upsetting our customers are finding this threat of a strike and we very much regret the disruption that the union's unjustified action will cause," BA Chief Executive Bob Ayling said.
T&G officials said earlier that the first of the cabin crew's planned three-day strikes appeared certain to go ahead after the latest round of talks collapsed.
BA is also in dispute with ground staff, who are protesting over the planned closure of BA's catering unit at Heathrow.
